details:
**Cyril Ramaphosa**
President of South Africa since February 2018 and leader of the African National Congress. He is a former trade unionist and businessman who succeeded Jacob Zuma.

**Jacob Zuma**
South Africa's president from 2009 until February 2018, when the ANC forced him to resign amid corruption scandals.

**African National Congress (ANC)**
The party of Nelson Mandela, which has governed South Africa since the end of apartheid in 1994. It is led by Cyril Ramaphosa and was previously led by Jacob Zuma.

**Gupta brothers and "state capture"**
Ajay, Atul, and Tony Gupta were Indian-born businessmen who had huge influence over Jacob Zuma's government, reportedly even shaping ministerial appointments. This corrupt arrangement is called "state capture."

**Julius Malema and the Economic Freedom Fighters**
Julius Malema leads the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), a radical left-wing party that demands faster seizure and redistribution of land from white owners to Black South Africans.

**"Dubul' ibhunu"**
An apartheid-era struggle song whose title means "Shoot the Boer." Julius Malema was condemned and taken to court for singing it at rallies, with critics saying it incites violence against white farmers.

**Democratic Alliance**
South Africa's main opposition party, which is liberal and centrist. It has condemned Malema and opposed the ANC. Since 2024 it has also joined the ANC in a coalition "Government of National Unity."

**Phala Phala scandal**
The scandal over large sums of foreign cash that were reportedly hidden in a couch at Ramaphosa's Phala Phala game farm and stolen in a 2020 burglary. It raised questions about whether he had violated currency and anti-corruption laws.

**"McBuffalo"**
A nickname for Cyril Ramaphosa, a wealthy businessman known for breeding exotic cattle and buffalo and for having held the McDonald's franchise in South Africa.

**NDZ (Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma)**
Jacob Zuma's ex-wife and a former African Union Commission chair. Cyril Ramaphosa narrowly defeated her in the December 2017 race for ANC leader.

**F. W. de Klerk and the 1994 transition**
F. W. de Klerk was the last apartheid-era president. He negotiated the end of white minority rule, which led to the 1994 election of Nelson Mandela. He also oversaw the dismantling of South Africa's nuclear weapons.

**Nuclear weapons program**
South Africa built a small nuclear arsenal during apartheid and then voluntarily dismantled it around 1990–1991, just before apartheid ended. It is the only country to have built nuclear weapons and then given them up entirely.

**Vela Incident**
A mysterious "double flash" detected by a U.S. Vela satellite over the South Atlantic in 1979. It is widely believed to have been a secret nuclear test carried out jointly by Israel and South Africa.

**Pelindaba**
The headquarters of South Africa's nuclear research program near Pretoria. It gives its name to the Treaty of Pelindaba, which made Africa a nuclear-weapon-free zone.

**BRICS and the 2023 Johannesburg summit**
South Africa joined the BRIC bloc (Brazil, Russia, India, China) in 2010, turning it into BRICS. It hosted the 2023 summit in Johannesburg, where Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov represented Russia because Vladimir Putin faced an International Criminal Court arrest warrant.
